rules: No prediction markets, random rewards, loot boxes, raffles or dice. Every reward must be deterministic, derived from behaviour or time.
Run 100% on the Fuji testnet or a mainnet fork. No real money, no real tokens, and no token sale to the public in any form.
Non-custodial by default: user funds stay in the user's own wallet or smart account. Pooled funds only where the topic says so, and only behind a multisig.
Agents (if any): a rule engine is mandatory and the LLM must never be the one deciding to move money. Every agent runs behind a policy contract with a spending cap, a whitelist and a kill switch.
On-chain data is limited to hashes, payments and state. No personal data, audio, transcripts or home addresses on-chain.
If a demo uses a dev toggle (simulated time, location or yield), declare it to the judges at the very start of the pitch.
Yield on testnet is mocked. The pitch must say where real yield would come from on mainnet (sponsor pool, blue-chip lending, service fees). Relying on newly printed tokens is not allowed.

Vietnamese law must be addressed in the pitch: crypto is not legal tender; salaries must be paid in VND; paid legal or financial advice requires a licence; tokenized stocks are geoblocked by their issuers. Teams that state the limits correctly earn points, teams that ignore them lose points.
Every team must be able to answer three questions in the pitch: why on-chain, why Avalanche, and where the money or yield comes from.
convention: Difficulty 1 = two people finish in one day, 5 = a team of three with experience using the full 48 hours. Required MVP = if it cannot be demoed, the project is not submitted. Bonus = extra points, not required. USDC in this document means testnet USDC on Fuji.

topics.title: Há»¥i on-chain (ROSCA)
topics.problem: Há»¥i is a popular rotating savings scheme in Vietnam, but it depends entirely on the organiser's reputation. Collapses happen often and players have no way to check where the money is.
topics.solution: A contract holds the USDC pool. Each round one member receives the pot, either on a fixed schedule or by bidding on interest (whoever needs money early pays interest to later receivers). Missing a round triggers an automatic penalty and every cash flow is public. The organiser becomes a contract, so nobody holds the money.
topics.why: Low transaction fees mean a group of 10-20 people paying weekly does not lose the pot to fees. Native USDC on the C-Chain.
mvp: Create a circle: number of members, amount per round, period, allocation mode (fixed schedule or bidding).
Pay in for a round, receive a round, penalty for late payment, close out and pay bidding interest.
Dashboard with each member's status and the transaction history.
topics.bonus: Sealed-bid bidding (commit-reveal), yield on the undisbursed part of the pool, invite members by link, sybil resistance with a Team1 attestation.

topics.title: Split-bill Vault
topics.problem: Friends on a trip, sharing a rented room or working on a group project always have someone who paid first and chases the money for weeks. Splitwise only records debts. It does not hold money and does not settle.
topics.solution: One vault per group. Members deposit USDC, whoever pays first logs an expense with the people it is split between, the contract computes net debts and settles everything in one transaction at the end. Unused balance flows into a yield mechanism and the interest is shared equally.
topics.why: Settling many small payments between 5-10 people needs near-zero fees, and blue-chip lending exists to park the balance.
mvp: Create a group, invite members, deposit and withdraw.
Log an expense, split equally or by ratio, compute net debts.
One settlement transaction for the whole group, with public history.
topics.bonus: Balance deposited into a mock yield vault, receipt photos hashed on-chain, custom split ratios, Telegram notifications.

topics.title: Commitment Stake
topics.problem: Student events and crypto meetups in Vietnam see 40-60% no-shows, and organisers who order food and seats for the registered number lose money. Free registration carries no cost of commitment.
topics.solution: Registering means staking 2-5 USDC into the event's contract. Checking in with a QR signed by the organiser on site refunds the deposit immediately. When the event ends, no-show deposits are split among attendees or go to the event fund, as the organiser chose in advance. While waiting, deposits sit in a yield vault.
topics.why: Refunding 200 people on site needs cheap, fast-confirming transactions, and Team1 runs its own events, so there are real users straight away.
mvp: Create an event: deposit, time, and what happens to no-show deposits.
Register with a stake, QR check-in signed by the organiser, automatic refund.
End of event: distribute no-show deposits by the chosen rule.
topics.bonus: Mock yield on deposits, automatic waitlist when someone cancels, partial refund if cancelling more than 24h ahead, proof-of-attendance NFT.

topics.title: Allowance Vault
topics.problem: Vietnamese students get money from home monthly, spend it in the first ten days and borrow from friends. Parents have no way to give it out evenly and see where it goes without controlling every coin.
topics.solution: A parent deposits once and the contract streams USDC weekly into the student's smart account. The account has a policy both sides agree on at setup: a weekly cap, limited emergency withdrawals, and a protocol whitelist if the student wants to earn interest. The part not yet streamed sits in a yield vault and the interest goes to the student, as an incentive not to withdraw early.
topics.why: Streaming weekly for 4-5 months needs low fees, and an embedded wallet works for parents who are not comfortable with crypto.
mvp: The parent creates a vault, deposits, and sets the stream schedule and policy.
The student claims weekly, with a dashboard for both sides.
Limited emergency withdrawal with a clearly logged reason.
topics.bonus: Mock yield on the unstreamed part, policy changes that need both signatures, automatic monthly report, several children in one vault.

topics.title: Transparent Charity
topics.problem: Charity-statement scandals in Vietnam have destroyed trust in personal funds. Donors do not know where money goes, and even honest funds have to post bank screenshots.
topics.solution: The fund is a contract. Donors deposit USDC and the board is a 3-of-5 multisig approving each disbursement against milestones announced beforehand (buy 500 gift packs, fix one classroom). Every expense comes with an invoice hash and photo, on a real-time public dashboard. Undisbursed money sits in a yield vault and that interest also goes to the fund and is shown publicly.
topics.why: The dashboard must read thousands of small donations without cost. An optional own L1 records a receipt for every expense at almost no cost.
mvp: Create a fund with milestones and a multisig.
Donate. A public dashboard shows the balance, milestone progress and a list of expenses with document hashes.
Disburse through the multisig, locked while a milestone's conditions are not met.
topics.bonus: Mock yield on waiting funds, donors vote to cancel a milestone and get a proportional refund, receipts on an own L1, PDF statement export.
topics.stack: Solidity + Foundry, Safe, Next.js, a simple indexer (Glacier API or a subgraph), IPFS for documents.
topics.tagline: A charity fund with automatic statements: it receives USDC, releases money by milestone through a multisig, every expense carries a receipt hash, and money waiting to be spent earns yield for the fund.

topics.title: Quadratic Funding for student projects and clubs
topics.problem: University funds for clubs and projects are handed out by connections or by whoever asks the loudest. A project many students care about but with no patron gets nothing.
topics.solution: Each round has a matching pool from sponsors (Team1, the university, companies). Projects register and students donate 1-5 USDC. At the end of the round the matching is split by the QF formula: the square of the sum of the square roots of donations, so 100 people giving 1 USDC each earn more matching than one person giving 100 USDC. Sybil attacks are blocked with a simple attestation.
topics.why: Hundreds of small donations in one round need near-zero fees, and Team1 already has a builder list to base attestations on.
mvp: Create a round, fund the matching pool, register projects.
Donate with an attestation, compute QF on-chain or off-chain with a proof, distribute at the end of the round.
Round dashboard: projects, number of supporters, expected matching in real time.
topics.bonus: Pairwise matching to resist collusion, a matching cap per project, attestation from a university email via ZK email or a Team1 signature, rounds with several pools.

topics.title: Streak-based gamified savings
topics.problem: Students have little motivation to save because the amounts are small and bank interest is invisible. Web2 savings apps only send reminders, with no real reward.
topics.solution: A shared pool where each person sets a deposit schedule (for example 5 USDC a week). Everyone's principal stays theirs and can be withdrawn at any time. The pool's yield is split by streak score: the longer the streak, the higher the weight. Missing a week resets the streak to zero, but principal is never lost. This is the version of a no-loss lottery with the gambling element removed.
topics.why: Small weekly deposits need low fees, and blue-chip lending provides real yield once on mainnet.
mvp: Set a deposit schedule, deposit on time, compute the streak on-chain.
A mock yield source, with yield distributed by streak weight at the end of each epoch.
Withdraw principal at any time, with a dashboard of streak and yield received.
topics.bonus: Aave or Benqi on a mainnet fork instead of the mock, NFT badges at streak milestones, friend groups with a shared streak, deposit reminders over Telegram.

topics.title: Streaming payroll + milestone escrow
topics.problem: Vietnamese freelancers and outsourcing teams are often paid late, or not at all, after delivering. Escrow through Upwork costs 10-20% in fees and has no streaming.
topics.solution: Two modes. Stream: the client deposits USDC and the contract streams per second to the freelancer, so when it stops the money stops, and neither side holds the other's money. Milestone: money goes into escrow per milestone, the freelancer submits a deliverable hash, the client has 72 hours to dispute, after which it auto-releases, and a disputed milestone goes to an arbiter.
topics.why: Per-second streaming creates many small claim transactions that need low fees, and native USDC settles with foreign clients.
mvp: Stream contract: deposit, stream per second, claim, stop, refund the unstreamed part.
Milestone contract: escrow, submit a deliverable hash, auto-release after the dispute window, basic dispute.
A two-sided dashboard with the amount ticking in real time.
topics.bonus: The arbiter is a multisig or a pool of staked arbiters, on-chain invoices, top up a stream without interruption, several freelancers in one contract.

topics.title: Capped-resale NFT tickets with yielding float
topics.problem: Scalpers at concerts and big events in Vietnam push prices up 3-5 times. Organisers hold ticket money for months without earning anything, and refunds after a cancellation are manual and slow.
topics.solution: Tickets are minted as NFTs that can only be transferred through the contract's marketplace at a capped price, with any excess going to the organiser or a fund. Ticket money goes into a yield vault until event day and the interest goes to the organiser. If the organiser cancels, the contract refunds everyone automatically. Check-in burns the ticket or marks it as used.
topics.why: Minting and reselling thousands of tickets needs low fees, and door check-in needs fast confirmation.
mvp: Create an event, mint tickets, buy with USDC.
A resale marketplace with a price cap that blocks transfers outside the marketplace.
Automatic refund on cancellation, and a QR check-in that changes the ticket's state.

topics.title: YieldGO
topics.problem: DeFi onboarding for students fails because they have to learn first and only then use it. LootGO proved that walk-to-earn attracts users, but it rewards with random memecoins, which does not build good financial habits.
topics.solution: A real map (the campus and sponsor venues) where chests spawn and open when you get within 30 m. There are three deterministic chest types: the Yield Chest auto-deposits a small amount from a sponsor pool into a vault in the user's name; the Quest Chest hands out a DeFi micro-task with a tutorial; the Sponsor Chest at a coffee shop needs a QR scan on site. Rarity comes from an exploration score and streak, with no dice, and only multiplies the APY boost and quest tier. Energy, chest-opening radius and Compass level come from the deposit streak and the USDC in the vault: holding a position for long makes you stronger, withdrawing drops your level.
topics.why: Game state (spawn, open, XP, energy) produces dense transactions and needs its own Game L1 with a freely distributed native token so gas is near zero. Real money stays on the C-Chain and ICM connects the two. Separating game state from real money is the right design, and only Avalanche makes it this clean.
mvp: A map PWA (MapLibre) with chests spawning around one campus and opening within a radius.
A Game L1 spun up with the Avalanche CLI: chests, opening, XP, streak.
A USDC vault on the C-Chain (mock yield).
One ICM flow: open a Yield Chest on the L1, deposit on the C-Chain, and the stats return to the L1.
A dev toggle that simulates location, declared to the judges.
topics.bonus: A Sponsor Chest with a QR proof-of-visit, a Territory layer (the top hex holding positions longest shares extra from the sponsor pool), Compass level, a leaderboard by hex, the Contract Deployer Allow List precompile on the L1.

topics.title: DeFi Farm
topics.problem: DeFi vaults are dry and users do not understand what a lock period or accumulating yield means. Vietnamese students remember farm games from their childhood, so a farm metaphor explains DeFi without reading docs.
topics.solution: Each player has a farm on the Game L1. Planting a seed is a deposit into a vault on the C-Chain and each crop type maps to one lock period (vegetables one week, rice one month, fruit trees three months). A longer lock gives a rarer crop and a higher multiplier. Crops grow in real time, harvesting is claiming yield, and pulling one up early is withdrawing principal, losing the multiplier but never the principal. Fully deterministic: no random drops and no random pests.
topics.why: Watering, harvesting and expanding land are dense transactions that need a Game L1 with near-zero gas. Real money stays on the C-Chain and ICM syncs deposits and crop state. It uses the same two-chain architecture as topic 10.
mvp: A Game L1 spun up with the Avalanche CLI: plots, crops, growth by block time.
A vault on the C-Chain with three lock tiers (mock yield).
One ICM flow: planting on the L1 deposits on the C-Chain, and harvesting claims the yield.
A 2D game frontend with a free pixel asset pack, and a demo that compresses time with a dev toggle.
topics.bonus: Expand land by holding positions longer, visit friends' farms, a seed exchange market (not a token), Aave or Benqi on a mainnet fork instead of the mock.

topics.title: AI agent treasury with on-chain guardrails
topics.problem: Every AI trading-agent demo today hands the LLM a private key with full power. One hallucination or prompt injection and everything is gone. There is no on-chain standard for limiting an agent.
topics.solution: The agent holds no funds. It only has a session key that can call the smart account's `PolicyModule`. The module checks every transaction: the token and protocol are on the whitelist, total spend in the last 24 hours is under the cap, slippage is under the threshold, and nothing is sent to an address outside the whitelist. A violation reverts. The owner has a kill switch that revokes the session key instantly. The agent runs a rule-based rebalance (target weights) and the LLM only writes the explanation.
topics.why: Frequent rebalancing needs low fees, and there are DEXes and lending markets to demo against on Fuji or a fork.
mvp: A smart account with a PolicyModule: daily cap, token and protocol whitelist, kill switch.
A rule-based agent rebalancing 2-3 tokens through a DEX, with every transaction going through the module.
An attack demo: a prompt injection tries to make the agent send money out and the module reverts.
A test suite covering every money path of the module.
topics.bonus: A timelock on policy changes, LLM explanation logs hashed on-chain, several agents sharing one treasury with separate caps, a violations dashboard.

topics.title: DeFi Copilot
topics.problem: Newcomers do not know what health factor, LP or slippage mean. Asking ChatGPT does not work because it cannot read a wallet and invents numbers. The Copilot reads real data and explains it without guessing prices.
topics.solution: A harness made of an LLM loop, tool calling and per-session memory. Read tools: balances, positions, LPs and transaction history through RPC or the Glacier API, DEX quotes, protocol TVL and APY, health factor. Write tools: swap, add liquidity, deposit into a vault, with every transaction confirmed by the user and passing through a simple allowance. Analysis comes only from verifiable on-chain data: at what price a position is liquidated, how much a whale just pulled from a pool. Price forecasts are forbidden. An eval set in Vietnamese and English measures intent parsing and how many transactions slip through the guardrails.
topics.why: There are enough protocols on Fuji or a fork to make the write tools real, and the precompile bonus is something only Avalanche allows.
mvp: A harness with 6-8 read tools and 2-3 write tools, with the user confirming every transaction.
Chat about portfolio risk, liquidation price and swap commands.
A 30-case eval set with a report of intent accuracy and how many wrong transactions were blocked.
topics.bonus: A custom precompile on Subnet-EVM that enforces the allowance at the protocol layer (needs Go), long-term memory, proactive alerts when health factor drops, an MCP server so other agents can call it.

topics.title: Tx Guardian
topics.problem: Vietnamese users lose money by approving unknown contracts and signing transactions from fake links. Wallets today show hex data that nobody can read.
topics.solution: A user pastes a transaction or connects a wallet through a small extension. The backend simulates it on an Anvil fork of the C-Chain and reads the state diff (which tokens leave, which come in, which approvals are granted). A rule engine flags unlimited approvals, unverified contracts, addresses that look like one you know (address poisoning), and drain patterns (moving the entire balance). An LLM writes the explanation from the state diff it already has, without guessing. The result comes with a warning level and a reject button.
topics.why: Forking the C-Chain is fast because block times are short, and verified contracts on the explorer give the rule engine something to look up.
mvp: Simulation on an Anvil fork that returns the state diff for swaps, approvals and transfers.
A rule engine with 5 rules: unlimited approval, unverified contract, address poisoning, drain pattern, abnormal slippage.
A plain-language explanation from the state diff, shown in the UI before signing.
topics.bonus: An extension that blocks signing at a high warning level, a community-contributed database of scam addresses with attestations, an MCP server so copilots and other agents can call it, hashes of check results on an own L1 as proof.

topics.title: StockAgent Launchpad
topics.problem: Tokenized US stocks are live on Avalanche (Securitize has tokenized its own SECZ shares, Dinari and the S&P Digital Markets 50 Index, tokenized US stocks through Pharaoh Exchange), but there is no verified agent layer for managing portfolios. Old-style Virtuals graduates agents by token price on a bonding curve, not by ability.
topics.solution: Agent creators publish a rule-based manifest (scheduled DCA, target-weight rebalancing, volatility targeting, drawdown stop) and price predictions are forbidden. A five-phase pipeline: Register (ERC-8004 identity + a USDC bond), then Paper (runs on a fork with real Pyth prices, each decision logged as a hash on-chain together with the rule that triggered it), then Graduate (drawdown within limits, zero policy violations, uptime), then Live (a backer grants a session key with a policy into their own smart account and the agent executes non-custodially), then Reputation (an attestation on 8004, bond slashed on violations). The leaderboard scores by Sharpe ratio, max drawdown and policy compliance, not raw profit.
topics.why: Tokenized stocks are already here, Pyth has equity feeds on the C-Chain, and cheap transactions allow frequent rebalancing.
mvp: A registry + bond + one rule-based agent (DCA + rebalance) on mock tokenized stocks (tSECZ, tAAPL) pegged to Pyth prices.
The Paper phase compressed with an accelerated clock, with a hash logged for every decision.
Graduation by published criteria, one backer granting a session key, and the agent placing one real order on Fuji.
A risk-adjusted leaderboard.
topics.bonus: An LLM explaining each order (the explanation hash is also logged), slashing, selling signals over x402, logs running on an own L1.

topics.title: x402 Micropayment Rails on Avalanche
topics.problem: The agent economy needs to pay per request without API keys or subscriptions. x402 already has 69,000 active agents and 165 million transactions, but Vietnamese developers have no lightweight SDK to wrap their APIs, and someone has to confirm the rails can settle on Avalanche.
topics.solution: A facilitator that verifies the USDC `transferWithAuthorization` (EIP-3009) signature and settles on-chain; a one-line SDK middleware for Express, FastAPI and MCP servers that returns `402` with an `accepts` array; and a client SDK so an agent signs and retries on its own. Demo: one paid API and one agent that pays for data by itself.
topics.why: Settling USDC is cheap and fast on the C-Chain, and it can extend to an own L1 for micro-transactions under 0.01 USDC.
mvp: A facilitator that verifies and settles on Fuji, with `/verify` and `/settle` endpoints.
Server middleware for one framework and a client SDK for agents.
A demo agent that calls the API, gets a 402, signs, retries and receives the data, with a real settlement transaction.
topics.bonus: Middleware for MCP servers, the upto scheme (pre-authorise a maximum, settle the actual amount), batch settlement to cut fees, a revenue dashboard for sellers.

topics.title: ActorBazaar
topics.problem: X402's Agentic.market and Circle's Agent Marketplace only list existing endpoints and charge up front per request. Apify hosts and runs code for you, but billing is Web2 and creators wait until the end of the month for payout. Nowhere hosts code, charges by real usage, settles instantly and lets agents buy without an account.
topics.solution: An Actor is a repo with an `actor.json` (input schema, pricing model, entrypoint) plus a Dockerfile or template. Four pricing models: pay-per-run (one x402 call before running), pay-per-result (deposit a maximum into a TaskEscrow, settle by the number of items, refund the rest), pay-per-event (the seller defines events and the runner emits signed ones), and rental (streamed per second, bonus). The runner executes the container with a timeout and resource cap, and the image digest is recorded on-chain so buyers know the published code is what runs. Receipts hash the input, output, usage and payment onto an own L1, and reputation comes from receipts. A Vietnamese-first catalogue: Actors for Vietnamese data and language.
topics.why: X402 settlement is cheap on the C-Chain, and an own L1 records the receipt of every run almost for free, which would not be possible on an expensive chain.
mvp: A registry + a Docker runner for one Node template + an input-schema form.
Pay-per-run over x402, a dataset output and an on-chain receipt.
Two sample Actors with Vietnamese data, and a web catalogue.
topics.bonus: Pay-per-result with a TaskEscrow, pay-per-event, an MCP server so agents can find and run Actors themselves, scheduling, rental streaming, hosted containers for long-running agents.

topics.title: TalkMeter
topics.problem: Otter and Fireflies charge 20 USD a month even if you only meet twice, and no product bills a 30-minute student group meeting for exactly 30 minutes. Most interview copilots on the market feed answers to candidates, and companies ban them.
topics.solution: The client cuts audio into 60-second chunks and each chunk calls a transcribe API. The server replies `402` with a price, the client signs USDC from a session budget, the facilitator settles and the transcript comes back. When the budget cap is hit, the copilot stops. At the end, the summary is a separate call, and a receipt hash for the whole session goes to an L1. Work-meeting mode: live Vietnamese and English transcript, action items with owners and deadlines. Interviewer mode: a scorecard by criteria, follow-up suggestions when a candidate answers vaguely, and flags for questions with bias risk. Mock-interview mode: the AI plays the interviewer and gives feedback at the end.
topics.why: Thirty settlements of 0.02 USDC in one meeting only pay off if gas is below the price of a minute, and an own L1 records the receipt of every minute almost for free.
mvp: Work-meeting mode: capture the mic, 60-second chunks, x402 on each chunk, live transcript.
A session budget cap that stops automatically, and a consent banner at the start of a session.
A summary + action items, with an on-chain receipt.
topics.bonus: An interviewer scorecard, mock interview, streaming payment (topic 8) instead of chunks to bill down to the second, buying a translation or crawling sub-agent from topic 18, pushing action items to topic 3.

topics.title: AskPay
topics.problem: Students ask legal questions every day (rental contracts, part-time work, traffic, academic rules) and ChatGPT invents laws with total confidence. The asker carries the hallucination risk while the seller loses nothing.
topics.solution: Two price tiers (quick 0.05 USDC, deep 0.2 USDC), with money going into an AnswerEscrow. A RAG pipeline answers with citation JSON `{document, article, clause, excerpt}`. The citation validator is ordinary code: the document exists in the corpus, the article and clause are real, the excerpt matches at least 90% of the source text, and the document is still in force. If it passes, the money is released. If any citation fails, the whole amount is refunded and the answer is labelled unverified. Hashes of the question, answer, citations and validator result go to an L1 so anyone can audit the hallucination rate. Tier 2: escalate to a real lawyer with a 5-20 USDC escrow, released on acceptance or after 48 hours.
topics.why: Automatic per-answer refunds of 0.05 USDC are only feasible when settlement is cheap, and an own L1 records the receipt of every question almost for free.
mvp: A corpus of 30 legal documents from the Government's legal-document portal, chunked by Article and Clause.
RAG + citation JSON, a validator + auto-refund, x402 with two tiers.
An on-chain receipt and a simple web chat.
topics.bonus: Lawyer escalation with escrow, a biology pack (open-access corpus, a validator that checks DOIs and excerpts against abstracts, scoped to literature review), an MCP server for other agents to ask, a public hallucination-rate dashboard, a pack marketplace with revenue share.

topics.title: PayrollFloat
topics.problem: Payroll money sits idle for 29 days every month. 500k USDC at 4-5% APY is 1,500-1,800 USD a month, small change for a payroll company handling 6 million USD a year but free money with no operational cost. No product does this with a hard deadline and a no-loss-of-principal guarantee.
topics.solution: A one-month lifecycle. T+1: receive the money, keep a 5% buffer, allocate by policy. T+2 to T-4: monitor utilisation and venue health. T-3: start unwinding on a ladder, never in one lump. T-1: everything must be back in the PayrollVault, and if not, the kill switch fires and the CFO is alerted. T: pay a batch (Merkle) or open streams. Interest is tracked separately and the platform fee comes out of the interest. The agent can only move money between whitelisted venues and the PayrollVault, with no path to an unknown wallet. Policy changes go through the company's multisig. The pitch is B2B SaaS taking 10-20% of yield across many companies.
topics.why: Blue-chip lending (Aave, Benqi) and yield-bearing stablecoins serve as venues, and rebalancing and unwinding many orders needs low fees.
mvp: A PayrollVault + FloatPolicy (whitelist, max 40% per venue, buffer, deadline rule, kill switch).
An agent that deposits into 2 mock venues, a LadderScheduler that unwinds, and a batch payment to 10 addresses.
A demo compressing one month into 10 minutes, with one scenario where a venue cannot be withdrawn from and how the agent handles it.
topics.bonus: Streams instead of a batch (topic 8), an LLM monthly report for the CFO, multi-tenant support for many companies, a CFO dashboard, a backstop line.
